subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should isolated cron setup keep the fixed 60s watchdog, use the bounded job-timeout-derived policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219, or wait for an operator-configurable watchdog design?
rationale: Current source still has the bug class, but changing the default setup wait changes availability behavior for stuck runners and config knobs have a high product bar in this repository.

options.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Merge the open PR after confirming that longer stuck setup occupancy is an acceptable reliability tradeoff for isolated cron jobs.

options.title: Require an operator knob
options.body: Ask for a config-backed design if deployments must tune setup timeouts differently across slow providers or loaded hosts.

options.title: Keep 60s pending more proof
options.body: Leave the current watchdog in place until maintainers get a live trace of the exact failing setup phase from affected deployments.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Merge the open PR after confirming that longer stuck setup occupancy is an acceptable reliability tradeoff for isolated cron jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged setup-timeout mitigation touched the same watchdog, timer, and gateway cron surfaces and is the strongest current history signal for this behavior.
